transcript:
Header: 2026-10-14 10:00 PDT | Duration: 52m | Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Miguel Santos (Redwood SE), Leah Park (Quantaco), Ravi Patel (Quantaco), Maya Singh (Quantaco), Tom (Data Eng)

Summary: Weekly POC sync focused on cost/unit economics. Reviewed tokens/sec per dollar, caching savings observed in initial runs, and batching tradeoffs for Quantaco's 3 production prompts. Agreed next steps to run focused benchmarks and share security docs.

Topics: cost per token, tokens/sec/$, KV cache hits, batching profiles (1, 4, 16), dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs, SOC2/KMS/audit logs, timeline for procurement.

Transcript: 
00:00 - Avery: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on, we got about 50 minutes today, we'll focus on the cost econ numbers and the caching / batching tradeoffs from last week's runs.
00:12 - Leah: Yep thanks, um so we got Ravi's results in, there's a bunch of numbers but the headline is we need to get tokens per second up to improve cost.
00:22 - Miguel: Cool, I'll start with what we measured. So we ran three profiles, baseline single-request (no batching), small batch (4), and large batch (16). On the 2k context baseline we saw ~1,100 tokens/sec on the test model variant and the cost ended up around $0.024 per 1k tokens after our rough calc.
00:44 - Ravi: Can you repeat that? 1,100 tps for baseline? That seems higher than our initial numbers.
00:49 - Miguel: Yeah it's a throughput number from the dedicated pool sim, there's some variance though — we observed 900 to 1,200 depending on sequence length.
00:58 - Maya: Quick question, are these measurements with prefix caching enabled?
01:03 - Miguel: Good catch — baseline I listed was without prefix caching. With KV/prefix cache enabled we saw a ~28% reduction in token compute for the same conversational flows, so effectively tokens/sec/$ improves by about that percent, because you get fewer new tokens to compute. Note, the transcriber may put K V cache as "K V cache" in the notes, sometimes it's split.
01:27 - Leah: So 28% is cache hit savings, is that consistent across prompts? Some of our prompts are quite dynamic.
01:33 - Miguel: It's variable. For our FAQ-style flows we saw up to 45% savings, transformed search-like queries only 10-12%. The total depends on hit rate. We used the sample set Leah shared.
01:45 - Ravi: For batching, what was latency impact? We care about p95 latency for the web UI.
01:51 - Miguel: Right, for batch of 4 median latency increased ~40ms, p95 increased ~120ms. For batch 16 median saw around +150ms and p95 ~400ms. If you need sub-300ms p95, we'd recommend batching max 8 for this model on the current instance types.
02:12 - Leah: Okay that makes sense. Our product team tolerates up to 300ms for the interactive feature, but background jobs can be slower.
02:18 - Avery: Also want to flag that batching increases tokens/sec and reduces per-token cost, but it also increases tail latency and can complicate timeout handling — we can do batching-aware fallbacks (we have automatic fallback to smaller batches for spikes).
02:32 - Tom: Sorry I'm a bit late, can someone share the spreadsheet link?
02:36 - Avery: I'll drop it in the chat after the call and attach to the CRM. It's the updated cost model with assumptions per-run.
02:42 - Miguel: Another nuance — quantization/variant matters. The slightly faster quantized variant we tested had slightly worse quality on the long-context prompts, so tradeoff between cost and quality still there.
02:54 - Maya: Did we try the multi-model routing? For cheaper model for initial pass, then fallback to higher quality?
02:59 - Miguel: We sketched that: route short prompts to the cheaper L2 model, longer/higher-quality prompts to L1. That routing saved ~12% overall cost on the sampled traffic but added some complexity for consistency and latency.
03:12 - Leah: Security/compliance question: procurement wants SOC2 docs and confirmation on KMS — do you provide customer-managed keys for Private or Dedicated?
03:20 - Avery: Yes, for Private deployments you can do customer KMS or HSM; for Dedicated we support KMS integration and can offer customer-managed keys for Enterprise. We'll upload the SOC2 and KMS whitepaper in the shared folder.
03:32 - Ravi: Also need audit log granularity — we need token-level request logs anonymized for audits. Is that standard?
03:38 - Miguel: We can provide request-level logs, redaction or PII filtering is configurable. For Dedicated there's more retention and you can ship logs to your S3/GCS. We'll include the audit log retention options in the doc.
03:49 - Leah: Great. On procurement, cost model question — the per-token price in your hosted plan vs reserved vs private — can you summarize?
03:57 - Avery: Short answer: hosted is on-demand priced, good for early proofing; Dedicated reserved capacity lowers unit cost substantially if you commit; Private has larger fixed fee but gives you control and the best data isolation. In the spreadsheet I added a "tokens/sec per $" column and scenarios for 20/50/80% cache hit rates.
04:14 - Ravi: For our expected load (peak 10k requests/min with average 300 tokens per request), what's the recommended commit?
04:21 - Miguel: Ballpark: at 300 tokens/request and 10k rpm that's 3M tokens/min or ~50k tokens/sec sustained. With current numbers and batching 8 we can get to about 35-45k tokens/sec per dedicated pod depending on model. So you might need 2-3 pods for peak, but we'll run the dedicated-run next week to validate.
04:44 - Maya: Can you break that down into $/month assumption?
04:47 - Avery: In the spreadsheet I showed scenario A/B/C — with Dedicated reserved at our mid-tier you get ~35-45% lower unit price vs hosted. I'll send the exact numbers; the summary is you'd probably save ~30% in unit cost at your scale if you commit.
04:58 - Leah: Any notable gotchas for caching when we have multi-tenant inputs? We sometimes have user-specific prefixes.
05:05 - Miguel: Prefix caching can be per-user keyed, but hit rates drop with personalization. One idea is to cache static parts of prompts (system & instructions) and treat user-specific tokens as dynamic. That gave us most of the benefit without violating privacy constraints.
05:22 - Ravi: Regarding the benchmark runs — what telemetry do you need from our side?
05:26 - Miguel: If you can provide a small replay dataset of 1k representative sessions (we'll send a spec), timestamped and with variable sequence lengths, we can run the bench and give you per-prompt tokens/sec, p50/p95 latencies, and cache-hit breakdown. Please scrub PII or we can accept hashed IDs.
05:40 - Tom: Will the bench simulate our traffic pattern or is it uniform?
05:44 - Miguel: We can do both. We'll run the replay as-is and a synthetic mix that represents peak. That will surface batching warmup and KV cold starts.
05:52 - Maya: For the procurement timeline — if we want to go Dedicated, how long to provision?
05:56 - Avery: For Dedicated reserved with standard images, typically 2-4 weeks for contractual and infra provisioning. Private/VPC can be longer depending on network approvals, usually 4-8 weeks.
06:05 - Leah: Ok. Sounds like we should do the dedicated throughput run next Tuesday and then have procurement talk on the 28th.
06:11 - Avery: Perfect. Quick recap of action items: Miguel to deliver detailed tokens/sec/$ comparison and batching scenarios, Ravi to run the in-house latency test and provide replay dataset, Avery to share security docs and updated spreadsheet.
06:25 - Ravi: One last thing — are there any known stability issues with long 8k contexts?
06:30 - Miguel: We ran 8k at low QPS and saw KV growth impacts on memory, we recommend quantized KV-friendly model variant and slightly more memory per pod. We'll include config knobs.
06:43 - Leah: Thanks all, this was helpful. See you next week.
06:47 - Avery: I'll follow up with the spreadsheet and SOC2 link, Miguel will send benchmarks. End.

Post-call Notes: Attachments to upload: cost-model-v2.xlsx, security-deck.pdf, benchmark-spec.md.

Recap/Next Steps (verbatim for CRM): "Redwood/Avery to send updated cost model and SOC2/KMS docs; Miguel to run tokens/sec/$ benchmarking for batching profiles and share results; Quantaco (Ravi) to run sample latency tests with prefix caching enabled and provide replay dataset; schedule dedicated throughput validation next Tuesday."
